The founding file reopened from the archive (1989, closed as ‘trust internal correspondence — confidential’). The Footscray branch brought the files from the previous countries together on a single board:

· United Kingdom, Germany: the first payments under the name ‘consultancy’.
· Japan: the Tokyo invoices. France: Lot 47 and the Delorme shipment.
· USA: the Chicago warehouse. Italy: the Naples port slips.
· Spain: the Santa Ana Foundation, chief adviser in 1989 Edda Varga.
· Canada: Laurentide’s ‘special programmes’.
· Australia: Pacific Liaison Trust; the Footscray market, the Flemington stable, the Maribyrnong marina, the tram tender, Liaison Freight, Hopkins Street.

Two signatures on the founding document: ‘E. V.’ and ‘M. Ashby-Cole, coordinator’.
The founding file, closed for forty-one years, was opened. Nine countries on one desk.
THE 1989 FILE — INTERNATIONAL LIAISON PROGRAMME

· Cause of death: hypoglycaemia from an insulin overdose.
· Two injection marks on the abdomen; both at an angle that doesn’t fit a right-handed self-injection, from behind or from the side.
· A mild sleeping drug in the blood; in the evening tea.
· Time of death: 20.30–21.30.
AUTOPSY REPORT

Docklands tower, 8 December:

· 19.02 — Victor Quinlan, lobby exit.
· 19.30 — Fiona Marlowe, lobby exit.
· 20.15 — Kiran Naidoo, lobby exit.
· No entry recorded for Victor Quinlan after 19.02.

Note: the fire stairs are not written to the card log; they only show up on the alarm panel.
BUILDING CARD LOG
The coordinator’s driver.
I drive the car; I don’t listen to the back seat.

Downstairs, in the car park, waiting for her. At half nine Victor Quinlan came to the car and said, ‘Margaret’s staying tonight; drop me at the airport.’ I did. On the way we stopped at a courier office; he handed over an envelope. International.
He rests his hands together on his knees as if holding a steering wheel.
Where were you in the evening?
Brodie Walsh — interview
In the car park the counsel tells the driver, ‘Drop me at the airport’; on the way they stop at a courier.
Brodie Walsh
Fiona Marlowe
Emeka Okeke
The fire stairs set off the alarm; it is closed on the panel as a ‘false alarm’.
The counsel drops by and says, ‘Don’t go tomorrow’; tea is drunk.

8 December 21.58, Docklands courier office:

· Sender: Victor Quinlan. Recipient: ‘E. V.’, Budapest, a PO box.
· Declared contents: ‘legal documents — 1 ledger’.
· Payment: Pacific Liaison Trust corporate card.
COURIER RECORD
By courier to Budapest
Where did the coordinator’s ledger go?
It stayed in the safe
Into the shredder

Thirty-eighth floor, the coordinator’s office:

· On the desk, an insulin pen; the dose turned to the maximum.
· The farewell note was printed from the office printer at 21.12; at that hour her heart may have been beating, but her hand could not have held a pen.
· Her safe open and empty. Beside it, a dust mark on a bookshelf: rectangular, the size of a ledger.
· Drug residue in the teacup; a second cup has been washed.
OFFICE EXAMINATION
It was recorded that the ledger was sent to Budapest.
The safe was empty.
There was no ledger paper in the shredder.
Kiran Naidoo was arrested; the account holder went free.
Victor Quinlan was arrested. The PO box in Budapest was found empty. The founding file was sent to the branches of nine countries; an international search began for ‘E. V.’
The death was ruled a suicide. The programme entered its forty-first year.
Yindi Marrawa was arrested; the ledger reached Budapest.
The 1989 founding file
Building card log
Courier record
Alarm panel and printer log
The IT manager left at 20.15 and told you whose account the deletion command came from.

He closed the fire stair alarm with his own account, the farewell note was printed from his own laptop, and he sent the ledger to Budapest in his own name. The card log doesn’t save him: the fire stairs aren’t written to the log.
The angle of the injections doesn’t fit her own hand, there is a drug in the tea, and the note was printed from another computer.
The journalist waited in front of the building; there is no record of her going upstairs.
SUSPICIOUS DEATH
BDA Melbourne — Footscray Branch
Docklands, Melbourne
Suspicious death
Cleaner
Building line opened: alarm panel, fire stairs, office printers.
LINE A — BUILDING
Money line opened: the Trust’s accounts, courier shipments, counsel’s payments.
LINE B — MONEY
Programme line opened: the ‘International Liaison’ correspondence and founding documents.
LINE C — PROGRAMME

A message Margaret Ashby-Cole sent Victor Quinlan on 7 December, backed up before it was deleted:

‘Victor, tomorrow I’m going to Footscray. The ledger comes with me. Tell Edda forty years is enough. The actuary in Montreal, the archivist in Williamstown, the woman on Hopkins Street. All of it went through my papers.’

Reply: ‘Let’s talk tomorrow morning. Let’s have a cup of tea this evening.’
THE COORDINATOR’S LAST MESSAGE
The coordinator’s assistant.

Her ledger. Forty years old. She wrote every country, every payment, in her own hand: London, Berlin, Tokyo, Paris, Chicago, Naples, Seville, Montreal, here. It was kept in her safe. We had tea in the evening; Victor dropped by too and said, ‘Don’t go to the branch tomorrow; Budapest doesn’t want it.’ I left at 19.30.
Her fingers find the button of her blouse.
What was Margaret going to bring?
I kept her diary for twelve years.
Fiona Marlowe — interview
Heart attack
She was sedated and given an insulin overdose
How did she die?
She took an overdose of her own insulin
IT manager.
Servers don’t lie; people make servers say things.
Kiran Naidoo — interview

Last night at 21.20 all of the coordinator’s files were wiped remotely. The delete command came from the legal department’s privileged account. Only Victor uses that account. The same account closed the fire alarm.
He takes off his glasses and rubs his eyes.
Did anything happen on the servers?
LIAISON  /  SUSPICIOUS DEATH
The programme’s regional coordinator was found dead at her desk the night before she was due at the branch.
FILE #073
Night security officer.

The cards are logged. But I’ll tell you something: the fire stair door on the thirty-eighth floor doesn’t need a card, it only raises an alarm; last night at 20.40 it went off, and on the panel it was closed as a ‘false alarm’. I didn’t close it. IT and legal have the authority to close it.
He turns down the volume on his radio.
Who came in and out of the building in the evening?
The cards are logged; the cameras are on.
Emeka Okeke — interview

· 20.40 — 38th-floor fire stair door opened; closed at 20.41 as a ‘false alarm’ (legal department account, Victor Quinlan).
· 21.12 — the ‘farewell note’ document printed from the coordinator’s printer; sending session: Victor Quinlan’s laptop.
· 21.24 — the fire stair door opened again.

Yindi Marrawa
Legal counsel to Pacific Liaison Trust.
My job is to make sure the papers are in order.
No.
The card log is clear: I left at two minutes past seven and never came back in. I wasn’t in the building.
I sent the ledger to Budapest. That’s where it belongs. You won’t find Edda; she never stands anywhere unsigned, but she never stands anywhere at all.

I came back up the fire stairs and closed the alarm from my own account. I put the drug in the tea; I turned the pen. My laptop printed the note. I opened the safe. For forty years I put the papers in order; if that ledger went to Footscray, there would be no papers left.
You killed Margaret.
I left at seven and went to the airport. Margaret was tired, alone, ill. You’ve read her note.
He straightens his tie with his fingertips.
Where were you in the evening?
Victor Quinlan — interview
7 December: The coordinator calls the Footscray branch and writes to the counsel, ‘I’m going tomorrow.’
21.12: He prints the farewell note from his own laptop; at 21.20 he wipes the files and takes the ledger from the safe.
19.02: He has his lobby exit written to the card log.
21.00: He turns the insulin pen to the maximum dose and injects twice.
21.58: The ledger sets off for Budapest, to ‘E. V.’ In Footscray, the phone doesn’t ring.
20.40: He comes back up the fire stairs and closes the alarm with his own account.
19.00: The counsel drops by for ‘a cup of tea’; a sleeping drug goes into the tea.

On the night of 8 December 2030, on the thirty-eighth floor of a tower in Docklands, Pacific Liaison Trust’s regional coordinator Margaret Ashby-Cole (63) was found dead at her desk. In front of her was a printed, unsigned farewell note. On 7 December the coordinator had called the BDA Footscray branch and said, ‘Tomorrow I’m bringing everything.’

The cleaner Tamsin Grey found the body at 23.50. The legal counsel Victor Quinlan, the assistant Fiona Marlowe, the IT manager Kiran Naidoo, the security officer Emeka Okeke, the driver Brodie Walsh and the journalist Yindi Marrawa, who was waiting in front of the building, are to be interviewed.
INCIDENT REPORT

Request the autopsy report
Request the building card log
Request the courier record
Request an examination of the office
Open the building line
Open the money line
Open the programme line
Request the coordinator’s correspondence
Request the alarm panel and printer log
The card log was a decoy. When the three lines and the archive came together, the files of nine countries landed on one desk.
This time the phone didn’t ring. Only an address was left on the desk.
Docklands — December 2030

For forty-one years Margaret Ashby-Cole wrote the ‘International Liaison Programme’s money in nine countries into her own ledger. When she decided to go to the Footscray branch, the legal counsel Victor Quinlan drugged her tea, left on his card and came back up the fire stairs, killed her with insulin, printed the note, wiped the files and sent the ledger to Budapest, to ‘E. V.’
Who killed Margaret Ashby-Cole?
FILE #073  /  BUBE MELBOURNE — FOOTSCRAY
Night cleaner.
The thirty-eighth floor is always cleaned last.

Her light was on, as always; Ms Ashby-Cole works late. This time her head was on the desk. Around nine in the evening I smelled the counsel’s cologne in the corridor; he’s the only one on this floor who wears that scent. But at nine I was on the thirty-seventh floor; I’m not sure.
She takes off her gloves and holds them in her palm.
What did you see when you went into the office?
Tamsin Grey — interview
File #073 — Liaison
Kiran Naidoo
Victor Quinlan
Nobody — she took her own life
Yindi Marrawa
Investigative journalist.
I’ve spent three years on this trust.

Margaret. She gave me an appointment, midnight; ‘I’ll show you before the branch,’ she said. She didn’t come. Yes, I’d been following her for three years; yes, sometimes I waited outside her door. But I never went upstairs.
She presses her notebook to her chest.
What were you waiting for in front of the building?
Yindi Marrawa — interview
Insulin pen
The coordinator’s insulin pen; the dose turned to the maximum, emptied twice.
Farewell note
A computer-printed, unsigned farewell note.
Courier receipt
An international courier receipt; destination Budapest.
